diagram_math_checks.justification: The local change-of-basis definition is P_{C<-B}=[id_V]_B^C, with j-th column [b_j]_C; hence its source is B coordinates and target is C coordinates.

diagram_math_checks.relation: kappa_C composed with id_V = (multiplication by P_{C<-B}) composed with kappa_B.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Evaluating both paths at v gives [v]_C and P_{C<-B}[v]_B, respectively; these are equal by Statement and proof step 1.1. Arrow orientations are right/right/down/down, with no reverse-map arrow ambiguity.

Proof steps 2.1 and 3.1 compute identity compositions through the two ordered coordinate bases in each order. P_{B<-C} maps C columns back to B columns. Every product is n by n and its rightmost map applies first. The original step 3.1 explicitly covers empty bases in M_0(F), so n=0 remains included.
